chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast until it was said, "He does not break his fast." Then he fasted one day and broke one day. Then he fasted on Mondays and Thursdays. Then he transitioned from that to fasting three days in the month: Thursday at the beginning of the month, Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month. And he used to say: "That is the fasting of the whole time (the entire month)."'

And my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'There is no one more hateful to me than a man to whom it is said, "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do such and such," so he says, "Allah will not punish me if I strive hard in prayer." It is as if he sees that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) left something of the excellence due to inability (or weakness) on His part.'
ai.seo_question: What was the progression of the Prophet's (SAWW) voluntary fasting schedule according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Prophet's (SAWW) gradual transition from intense voluntary fasting to a sustainable 'fast of David' pattern, establishing a normative model for consistency over intensity. Imam Ali (AS) adds a crucial Shia scholarly insight: critics who claim the Prophet abandoned a practice due to inability (laziness) rather than preference (wisdom) are fundamentally misunderstanding the nature of prophetic excellence and the balance between obligatory duties and supererogatory acts.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Slih, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was Fasting such, until it was said, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> would not be breaking (not Fasting)’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> Fasted one day, and broke one day. Then he<sup>saww</sup> Fasted Mondays and Thursdays. Then he<sup>saww</sup> transferred from that to the Fasting of three days during the month, the first Thursday at the beginning of the month, and Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month; and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘That is the Fasting of the whole time (whole month)’.

And my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘There is no one more hateful to me<sup>asws</sup> than a man to whom it is said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to do such and such’, so he is saying, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not Punish me if I strive hard regarding the Prayer’. It is as if he sees that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> neglected something from the preferential acts being frustrated from it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, continued fasting for such a long time that people thought he was not to discontinue his fasting. He then discontinued fasting for such a long time that people thought he did not intend to fast anymore. He then would fast one day and eat the next day. He then fasted every Monday and Thursday. Then he would fast three days every month, Thursday of the beginning of the month, Wednesday of the middle of the month and the last Thursday of the month. He would say, “It is like fasting forever.’”

My father would say, ‘There is no other thing more hateful to me than one to whom it is said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, did this, but he says, “Allah will not punish me if I tried to perform Salat (prayer)” as if he thinks the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, neglected some of the virtuous acts because of his failure.’”
